summary.intent: Investigate and fix someguy v0.11.1 IPNS routing failures on staging (where IPNS endpoints hung indefinitely), then deploy a working someguy sidecar with delegated-ipfs.dev fallback and Prometheus metrics.
summary.outcome: Someguy sidecar fixed via corrected Docker config (libp2p port, accelerated DHT, proper memory), fallback routing with metrics implemented, and all 83 SDK E2E tests passing on staging with 15.28 ops/s throughput — 12x improvement over Phase 18 baseline. Release-please was also unblocked after extensive debugging by switching to `include-component-in-tag: true`.

repo: Someguy image ships `curl` but NOT `wget` — confirmed via `docker exec cipherbox-someguy which wget/curl`; healthchecks using `wget` fail inside the container.
`SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY` expects a raw uint64 byte count, not human-readable strings like '1GB' — silently causes crash-loop on startup.

The `DelegatedRoutingClient.publishRecord()` is fire-and-forget (detached promise). DB is always written synchronously first, so the DB always has a higher sequence number and wins every resolve comparison — 100% of IPNS resolves are served from DB.

Phase 18 baselines show 74% DB fallback rate even then; someguy doesn't change this architecture. Full throughput comparison: Phase 18 had 1.25 ops/s with 4.6% error rate; staging someguy achieves 15.28 ops/s with 0% errors.
`THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET` was not configured on staging — all initial E2E test runs against staging returned 429s. Secret must be passed as `x-throttle-bypass` header per `ThrottlerBypassGuard`.
Vitest does NOT auto-load `.env` files into `process.env` — env vars must be passed explicitly on the CLI (e.g. `THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET=x vitest run`).
Release-please multi-package Merge plugin always generates `chore: release main` as the PR title regardless of `pull-request-title-pattern` — the pattern config was irrelevant.

`include-component-in-tag: false` is functionally broken in release-please multi-package mode: release-please creates `v{version}` tags but its own release scanner cannot match them back to the root package path. Switch to `include-component-in-tag: true` with explicit component name.

Staging pre-release GitHub Releases with `v*-staging*` tags were being parsed by release-please as component `staging` with version `rc-1`, polluting the release scanner — 30+ such releases needed to be deleted.

`autorelease: pending` label must be manually corrected on merged release PRs whenever release-please fails to tag them; without this, all subsequent runs abort with 'untagged merged release PRs outstanding'.
`packages/crypto` was missing from both `release-please-config.json` and `.release-please-manifest.json` despite being an independently versioned package.

code.finding: resolveRecord() tries delegated routing first, then ALWAYS queries DB regardless. When both return results, it picks the higher sequence number — DB always wins because publishRecord() writes to DB synchronously before the fire-and-forget DHT publish completes.

Rewritten to support primary/fallback routing: DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL is primary (someguy), DELEGATED_ROUTING_FALLBACK_URL is fallback (delegated-ipfs.dev). Primary exhausts all retries before fallback is attempted. Backend type constrained to 'primary' | 'fallback' union.

Two new Prometheus counters added: cipherbox_delegated_routing_requests_total{operation, backend, outcome} and cipherbox_delegated_routing_fallbacks_total{operation}. Alert on rate(fallbacks[5m]) > 0 to surface frequent someguy failures.
No dotenv/envFile configuration — vitest does not load .env automatically. This caused throttle bypass secret to not be picked up even after creating tests/sdk-e2e/.env.
Someguy working config: expose port 4004/tcp+udp for libp2p inbound, DHT_ACCELERATED_DHT=true, SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY=1073741824 (bytes), 2GB container memory, 1.0 CPU, connection limits 100/3000.

workflow: Vitest env vars must be passed explicitly on the CLI or via vitest config `env` block — creating a .env file in the test directory is not sufficient.

When release-please fails to tag a merged release PR, the fix sequence is: (1) manually create the missing git tag and GitHub release, (2) flip the PR label from autorelease:pending to autorelease:tagged, (3) re-run the release-please workflow.

In multi-package release-please with the Merge plugin, `include-component-in-tag: true` with an explicit component name is required for the root package — bare `v{version}` tags are not reliably matched back to the root path by the scanner.

Staging pre-release GitHub Releases should not use a tag format that matches `{component}-v{version}` — they pollute release-please's scanner. Format `staging-{component}-v{version}-rc-{n}` (e.g. `staging-cipher-box-v0.26.5-rc-1`) is safe because `staging-cipher-box` is not a configured component.

When comparing load test results for a new IPFS routing backend, ensure the sidecar has been running for hours first — a cold DHT routing table (freshly started) gives 40-50% worse latency than a warm one, which skewed the initial local vs delegated-ipfs.dev comparison.
Docker healthchecks using CMD-SHELL run inside the container, not on the host — tools available on the Docker host are irrelevant. Always verify with `docker exec <container> which <tool>`.

friction: Release-please deadlocked repeatedly across the session due to: staging tag format collision (v*-staging* matched root package pattern), missing tags on manually-labeled PRs, and the fundamental `include-component-in-tag: false` scanner bug — required ~15 investigative iterations to fully resolve.
`SOMEGUY_LIBP2P_MAX_MEMORY=1GB` caused silent crash-loop on staging — no validation error at config parse time, just an indefinite restart loop discovered only by SSHing into the VPS after deploy.
SSH to staging VPS required 1Password agent approval which was not auto-granted, blocking several automation steps until the user confirmed the approach.
`THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET` not configured on staging caused all initial SDK E2E test runs to fail with 429s before the root cause was identified.
30+ old-format staging releases (`v*-staging-rc-*`) had to be individually deleted after being identified as a red herring in the release-please investigation.
Several release-please PRs (#331 in particular) generated changelogs covering the entire 600+ commit history due to missing anchor releases, requiring manual cleanup.
The `component: ''` config attempted in PR #330 did not fix the release scanner issue — it was a dead end that still needed the `include-component-in-tag: true` change in PR #333.
Background bash tasks in the session created race conditions where stale task notifications required reading output files to determine if they were already handled.
open_items: Mock IPNS routing service still present in local docker-compose even though someguy now covers all local dev routing needs — potential cleanup candidate.
DB-first IPNS resolution means someguy is never used for resolves in normal operation; a future optimization would return network results when sequence numbers match DB, reducing DB load.
No Grafana dashboards yet for the new delegated_routing_requests_total and delegated_routing_fallbacks_total metrics — need panels and an alert rule for fallback rate.
PR #335 (wiring THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET into staging deploy workflow) needs to merge and deploy — until then, a future staging deploy will overwrite .env.staging and break E2E tests again.

`packages/crypto` version jumped to 0.26.0 by absorbing all historical commits in a single release-please run — the CHANGELOG for that package contains fabricated history rather than actual changes per release.

Phase 18 vs Phase 19 performance baselines use different measurement methodologies (server-side Prometheus histogram vs full client round-trip SDK latency) — a direct apples-to-apples comparison would require adding the same Prometheus histogram instrumentation to the new someguy path.

Someguy `SOMEGUY_IPNS_ENDPOINTS` fanout-to-delegated-ipfs.dev option was evaluated but rejected (concurrent fanout not fallback, no per-source metrics) — worth revisiting if the API-level fallback proves insufficient.
